title: Rate limiter: 10 requests per minute
summary: A burst of parallel API calls slips past a per minute quota.
background: An API sells plans with a quota, for example 10 requests per minute per API key. Every accepted request is logged in requests, and before accepting a new one the gateway counts the requests of that key in the last minute.

The naive gateway runs SELECT count(*) and, if the count is under the limit, inserts the new request. A client that fires 40 calls in parallel makes all of them count at the same moment, all see a number under 10, and all get accepted. Counting rows cannot lock rows that do not exist yet, so row locks on requests do not help.

The fix is to serialize the decision per key. Lock the api_keys row with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE, or take a transaction scoped advisory lock with pg_advisory_xact_lock(key_id), then count and insert. Requests of other keys run in parallel, requests of the same key queue for a few microseconds. At larger scale the counter moves to a single row per key and window updated atomically.

race.goal: Key 1 is on a plan of 10 requests per minute. 20 clients send 2 requests each in the same second. At most 10 may be accepted.

inner.title: Requests with key, org and plan
inner.prompt: Join requests, api keys, organizations and plans for a full request log.

left.title: Usage per key, including zero
left.prompt: List every api key with its requests in the last day. Unused keys must show 0.

right.title: Plans nobody uses
right.prompt: List every plan with its api keys, keeping plans that have no key.

full.title: Documented versus called endpoints
full.prompt: Match the endpoint catalog with the paths seen in requests, showing undocumented calls and endpoints never called.

cross.title: Per minute usage grid
cross.prompt: Build every api key x minute of the last 5 minutes grid and count the requests in each cell.

self.title: Organization hierarchy
self.prompt: Show every organization next to its parent organization.

semi.title: Organizations that got throttled
semi.prompt: Return organizations with at least one key that received a 429.

anti.title: Keys never used
anti.prompt: Return api keys that never made a request.

lateral.title: Last two calls per key
lateral.prompt: For every api key return its two most recent requests.
